title: Contain Dresser export timeout and child cleanup
goal: A real browser-backed Dresser export timeout returns a bounded MCP error without terminating Node, and every Chrome and mirror child created by that render is stopped with its disposable state removed.

delivery.user_value: An agent can recover from a stalled Dresser PNG download without losing the MCP server or leaving local browser and mirror processes behind.

steps: Run the targeted live timeout regression with the exact local mirror and a real controlled Chrome process.
Reach Dresser's exportPng/download wait, induce a bounded download timeout, and observe a stable MCP error while Node remains alive.
Verify the test-created Chrome and mirror PIDs are gone, their loopback port is closed, disposable profile/download directories are removed, and no partial PNG exists.

work_classification.reason: This remediation changes internal promise and child-process lifecycle handling only; it does not alter product flow, screen structure, navigation, or defaults.

local.reason: The approved MCP MVP and its single remediation remain local-only with no Discord or external tracker writes.

reasons: The fix changes timeout and process-lifecycle behavior at the browser integration boundary, but is local, reversible, and does not change the public preset or artifact contract.

out: MCP tool names, input/output schemas, dresser-preset/v1, capability discovery, normal render semantics, artifact metadata, and stable error codes
server/mockup-mcp/server.mjs, server/mockup-mcp/preset-schema.mjs, server/mockup-mcp/dresser-preset-v1.schema.json, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, and README changes
changes to any file or asset inside .local/dresser-mirror
changes to /tools/mockup or any portfolio interface
new rendering features, Figma ingestion, multi-screen composition, batch rendering, video work, public transport, deployment, publication, and Git push
fixing the accepted full-repository lint debt or any unrelated dirty-worktree file

constraints: Fix only the verified race in which the timeout-bearing Browser.downloadWillBegin promise can reject before exportPng attaches its handler, plus the cleanup path needed to contain that failure.

Attach rejection handling to every started timeout/download promise immediately, await it in a structured try/finally path, and preserve the existing bounded DOWNLOAD_FAILED public error rather than allowing an unhandled rejection or process exit.

Guarantee idempotent cleanup for every session outcome: close CDP/browser resources, stop only the Chrome and mirror child processes created by that session, wait for termination with a bound, escalate only for those owned PIDs when necessary, and remove disposable profile/download directories while preserving completed intentional PNG artifacts.

The regression must launch the exact loopback .local/dresser-mirror and a real controlled Chrome session, load a valid source and preset, reach the actual exportPng/download branch, and induce the timeout there; replacing launch with an immediate throwing stub does not satisfy this task.

Any test-only timeout seam must remain internal to browser-session.mjs, must not change the MCP surface or normal runtime defaults, and must provide observable proof that the export action occurred before timeout handling and cleanup assertions.
Do not kill, reuse, or inspect unrelated Chrome processes or the user's existing mirror on port 5173; tests must use their own child PIDs, disposable directories, and loopback port.

Preserve every non-blocked behavior and security boundary frozen in TASK-MOCKUP-MCP-001, including loopback-only traffic, redacted errors, unique non-overwriting outputs, serialization, mirror integrity, and the accepted 10-error full-repository lint baseline.

Preserve unrelated dirty-worktree changes. Do not edit generated dist files, task history, original task/audit evidence, or perform Git push, deployment, publication, force-push, merge, tag, or release.
acceptance_criteria: When a real Dresser PNG export reaches its Browser.downloadWillBegin wait and times out, the promise is already rejection-handled, Node remains alive, and dresser_render_png returns the existing bounded DOWNLOAD_FAILED MCP error with no unhandledRejection or uncaughtException.

After that timeout, the exact Chrome and mirror child PIDs created for the render have exited, the test loopback port no longer accepts connections, CDP is closed, disposable profile/download directories are absent, and no partial or stale PNG is returned or left in the final output root.

An automated live regression launches the exact local mirror and real Chrome, loads a valid screenshot/preset, proves the Dresser export action was invoked, induces the export/download timeout after launch, asserts the bounded error and server liveness, and verifies cleanup without replacing launch with an immediate throwing stub.

Existing live success, solid/mesh rendering, capability discovery, sequential isolation, BUSY behavior, source/preset negatives, and unavailable-browser/mirror errors continue to pass with unchanged public MCP schemas, dresser-preset/v1, artifact metadata, and stable codes.

Only browser-session.mjs and mcp-live.test.mjs change; mirror integrity, task-scoped MCP lint/tests/build, diff validation, and the strict no-regression comparison to the accepted full-repository lint baseline pass.

checks.description: Outside the unit-test process, run the real BrowserSessionManager against the exact mirror with a valid screenshot/preset and a bounded export-stage timeout; record export invocation, caught DOWNLOAD_FAILED, continued process liveness, and absence of unhandled rejection or exception.

Record the remediation run's owned Chrome and mirror PIDs, loopback port, profile path, and download path without exposing user source paths; after timeout verify both PIDs are gone, the port is closed, disposable directories are absent, and unrelated Chrome plus the user's port-5173 mirror were untouched.

Re-run stdio tool discovery, live capabilities, and one successful PNG render; compare tool schemas, dresser-preset/v1, stable codes, artifact fields, and successful cleanup with TASK-MOCKUP-MCP-001 evidence.

Inspect the scoped diff and run full pnpm lint as a no-regression comparison; require changes only in the two in-scope files and exactly the accepted 10 errors in the same five out-of-scope files with no MCP finding.

steps: Revert only the TASK-MOCKUP-MCP-001-R1 changes in server/mockup-mcp/browser-session.mjs and server/mockup-mcp/tests/mcp-live.test.mjs.
Stop only any R1 test-owned child process still identified by its recorded PID, remove only its disposable test directories, and rerun the original task-scoped MCP checks.
data_recovery: No migration or source-data mutation exists; failed-render files are disposable, and successful pre-existing PNG artifacts remain untouched.

visual_gate.reason: This remediation changes browser promise and child-process cleanup internals only and has no visible interface or UX-flow impact.

evidence_required: bounded DOWNLOAD_FAILED and MCP process-liveness evidence
owned Chrome and mirror PID termination plus closed-port evidence
disposable profile/download cleanup and no-partial-artifact evidence
unchanged MCP contract and successful-render regression
task-scoped tests, lint, build, mirror-integrity, and diff logs
two-file scoped diff and unchanged full-repository lint debt comparison

history.summary: Contain the real Dresser export timeout and always clean up task-owned Chrome and mirror child processes.
